title: The Battle of Tours
description: October 732. Charles Martel's Frankish infantry must hold the wooded high ground between Tours and Poitiers against the Umayyad cavalry of Abd al-Rahman. A third force of Aquitanian allies under Duke Odo can be rallied to strike the enemy camp. Victory requires repelling the cavalry charges and forcing the invaders' withdrawal.

anachronisms_found: WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR stands in for Charles Martel — a Norman duke of 1066, 334 years after Tours, and mounted rather than the dismounted Frankish commander the dialogue describes
SALADIN represents Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi — an Ayyubid Kurd of the 1180s, four and a half centuries too late and from the wrong dynasty/theatre
EL_CID represents Duke Odo of Aquitaine — a Castilian of the 1090s; a generic Frankish/Aquitanian hero or simple named cavalry would have been far less misleading

Player Two's camp is a stone CASTLE with 99 STONE_WALL segments and 4 GUARD_TOWERs; the Umayyad force was a mobile raiding army whose camp was a tented laager, and the historically decisive raid on it worked precisely because it was unfortified
PIKEMAN x8 for the Franks — the pike formation is a 14th-century development; the spearman/champion mix alone would have carried the shield-wall idea
12 CAMEL_RIDERs in the Loire valley overstates camelry; Abd al-Rahman's mounted arm was Arab and Berber horse
MONASTERY buildings on both sides in 732 (an Umayyad monastery especially) are out of place

issues_found: Charles Martel is represented by the WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR hero — a Norman duke of 1066, over three centuries later and of the wrong polity; a renamed generic Champion or Teutonic-style infantry hero would have been correct and was available.
Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi is represented by SALADIN, an Ayyubid sultan of the 1170s-90s, not an Umayyad governor of al-Andalus in 732 — wrong dynasty and wrong century.
Duke Odo of Aquitaine is represented by EL_CID, an 11th-century Castilian; wrong person, wrong century, wrong region.

Both active players are set to RANDOM civilization, so Frankish and Umayyad architecture, unit rosters and bonuses are left to chance rather than assigned (Franks and Saracens/Berbers being obvious choices).

The Umayyad raiding column is given a CASTLE, 99 STONE_WALL segments, a gate and 4 GUARD_TOWERs — the invaders were a mobile plundering army with a wagon-and-tent camp, not a fortified stone position; the TENT/PAVILION camp objects were correctly used for Odo's force but not for the enemy.
Player 1 defeat is tied to loss of a TOWN_CENTER; the Franks fielded a field army on wooded high ground, they had no town centre to lose at the battle site.
CAMEL_RIDER x12 overstates camelry: the Andalusi/Berber force was overwhelmingly horse cavalry with some light infantry.

Charles Martel is represented by WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR, a Norman duke of 1066 — over three centuries after Tours; a renamed generic Champion or Teutonic-style infantry hero would have been correct and was available.
Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi is represented by SALADIN, a 12th-century Ayyubid Kurd of an entirely different polity and era than the Umayyad governor of al-Andalus.
Duke Odo of Aquitaine is represented by EL_CID, an 11th-century Castilian — wrong century and wrong realm; Odo was the Frankish/Aquitanian duke who had already fought at the Garonne.

Both active players are set to RANDOM civilization, so Frankish and Andalusi/Berber architecture and unit availability are left to chance rather than assigned (Franks and Saracens were both available).

The Umayyad camp is built as a CASTLE with 99 STONE_WALL segments and 4 GUARD_TOWERs; Abd al-Rahman's force was a raiding army encamped in the open with a baggage/plunder train, not a stone fortress in Gaul.
12 CAMEL_RIDERs for the Umayyad host at Tours; the invading force in Aquitaine was horse cavalry, and camels are a gratuitous orientalisation given Light Cavalry/Knight substitutes exist.
PIKEMAN among the Frankish line is a Late-Medieval anachronism for 732, though within the engine's abstraction of a shield wall.
The Aquitanian ally (player THREE) fields only 15 men and three tents with no real camp presence, understating Odo's role.
